evidence.claim: Khamenei said Iran's economy should not be tied to efforts to remove U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy and foreign trade.
evidence.title: Iran's Khamenei says economy should not be tied to U.S. sanctions
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei said Iran's economy should not be tied to efforts to remove U.S. sanctions and urged officials to govern so sanctions would not hurt the country, while promoting a knowledge-based economy and foreign trade.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters summary and quoted speech in the article text
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters wire quotes the supreme leader directly in a target-period speech.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target period, March 21, 2022 Nowruz speech.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Khamenei speech; strong ruler attribution.
contrary_evidence: A speech states intent and framing, not implementation or results.

evidence.claim: Khamenei used his New Year speech to call for knowledge-based production, job creation, higher productivity, and food self-sufficiency, saying production would improve growth, employment, inflation, and public welfare.
evidence.title: Leader: Iran's economy should not be tied to US sanctions, country must become impervious to bans
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei used his New Year speech to call for knowledge-based production, job creation, higher productivity, and food self-sufficiency, saying production would improve growth, employment, inflation, and public welfare.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official outlet quoting a televised speech with direct quotations; useful for intent but not independent on effects.
evidence.period_fit: Exact target period, March 2022 New Year message and follow-up speech.
contrary_evidence: Official state-media framing may overstate policy coherence and success.

evidence.claim: As of 28 February 2022, Iran had reported more than 6.6 million COVID-19 cases and about 140,000 deaths; WHO and partners helped mobilize more than 130 million vaccine doses, expand genomic sequencing, and support refugees and displaced people in the response.
evidence.title: Response to COVID-19 in Iran
evidence.excerpt: As of 28 February 2022, Iran had reported more than 6.6 million COVID-19 cases and about 140,000 deaths; WHO and partners helped mobilize more than 130 million vaccine doses, expand genomic sequencing, and support refugees and displaced people in the response.
evidence.source_locator: Country story, opening paragraphs under "Increased vaccination coverage and surge in genomic sequencing capacity"
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official WHO country story with dated, country-specific figures and explicit response description.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 target year and the immediate pre-2022 pandemic context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial and structural: this describes state pandemic response capacity under the regime, not a specific Khamenei order.
contrary_evidence: The same source says low vaccination coverage and sanctions constrained the response, so the picture is mixed.

evidence.claim: UNICEF and the Ministry of Cooperatives, Labour and Social Welfare presented Iran's child social protection system, including a welfare database that records deprived households and a cash-plus approach in selected provinces for vulnerable children and lactating mothers.
evidence.title: UNICEF and Ministry of Labour discussed enhancing social protection systems for children
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF and the Ministry of Cooperatives, Labour and Social Welfare presented Iran's child social protection system, including a welfare database that records deprived households and a cash-plus approach in selected provinces for vulnerable children and lactating mothers.
evidence.source_locator: Body paragraphs describing the webinar presentations and the welfare database / cash-plus scheme
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official dated program note with concrete implementation details from the government side and UNICEF partnership side.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: this describes state social-policy machinery under the regime, not direct personal action by Khamenei.
contrary_evidence: The need for targeted database-backed assistance implies substantial deprivation and incomplete coverage.
The page is programmatic rather than an outcome evaluation.

evidence.claim: UNICEF supported health screening for 97,454 children, including refugee children, and said that more than one million children participate annually in school-readiness screening; the programme also supported Afghan refugee, nomad, and low-income-area children.
evidence.title: برنامه سنجش سلامت برای کودکان پناهنده افغان
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF supported health screening for 97,454 children, including refugee children, and said that more than one million children participate annually in school-readiness screening; the programme also supported Afghan refugee, nomad, and low-income-area children.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and middle paragraphs on the screening programme
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated and quantified, with a clear vulnerable-group focus and an identified delivery mechanism.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: this is an education/health screening partnership under state institutions, not direct Khamenei action.
contrary_evidence: The page shows the need to extend screening to refugees and low-income areas, which indicates persistent inequality.

evidence.claim: Afghan refugee inflows were putting intense pressure on education infrastructure; access was also constrained by economic and geographic barriers, transport shortages, and gender disparities, while UNICEF was working with the Ministry of Education and partners to expand classrooms, rehabilitate WASH facilities, promote inclusive education, and improve emergency preparedness.
evidence.title: Education for Refugees
evidence.excerpt: Afghan refugee inflows were putting intense pressure on education infrastructure; access was also constrained by economic and geographic barriers, transport shortages, and gender disparities, while UNICEF was working with the Ministry of Education and partners to expand classrooms, rehabilitate WASH facilities, promote inclusive education, and improve emergency preparedness.
evidence.source_locator: Sections titled "The issue faced", "The actions taken", and "The impact sought"
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official program page with concrete program content, but undated and more contextual than evaluative.
evidence.period_fit: Relevant to 2022 inherited conditions and ongoing response, though the page itself is current.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial and structural: it documents state/UNICEF cooperation and barriers, not a direct Khamenei decision.
contrary_evidence: The page explicitly says access is restricted by economic/geographic barriers and that school quality and breadth are adversely affected.

evidence.claim: UNICEF says aging and insufficiently maintained water infrastructure, worsened by climate change, is strongly affecting vulnerable populations in Iran, and that it works with the government to ensure WASH access for children, vulnerable households, refugees, and host communities, including emergency preparedness and primary health-care hygiene.
evidence.title: Water, Hygiene and Sanitation
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF says aging and insufficiently maintained water infrastructure, worsened by climate change, is strongly affecting vulnerable populations in Iran, and that it works with the government to ensure WASH access for children, vulnerable households, refugees, and host communities, including emergency preparedness and primary health-care hygiene.
evidence.source_locator: Sections titled "The issue faced" and "The actions taken"
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official program page with clear intervention descriptions, but undated and not outcome-evaluated.
evidence.period_fit: Relevant to 2022-2023 conditions and ongoing services.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial and structural: it reflects the delivery system and UN partnership rather than a direct Khamenei order.
contrary_evidence: The page emphasizes scarcity and infrastructure stress, so it is evidence of need as well as response.

evidence.claim: UNICEF says year-on-year food-price increases above 50 percent are making quality nutrition less affordable for vulnerable groups, and that a 2021-2022 survey in eight food-insecure provinces found widespread zinc and vitamins A/D deficiencies among children under five; UNICEF is supporting targeted surveillance and supplementation for at-risk groups.
evidence.title: Child Nutrition
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF says year-on-year food-price increases above 50 percent are making quality nutrition less affordable for vulnerable groups, and that a 2021-2022 survey in eight food-insecure provinces found widespread zinc and vitamins A/D deficiencies among children under five; UNICEF is supporting targeted surveillance and supplementation for at-risk groups.
evidence.source_locator: Sections titled "The issue faced" and "The actions taken"
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official page with specific quantitative claims and a 2021-2022 survey reference that is directly relevant to the target period.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant because it references a 2021-2022 survey and the 2022 nutrition environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial and structural: it documents the nutrition response system, not direct Khamenei personal direction.
contrary_evidence: The same page shows substantial food-price inflation and ongoing micronutrient deficiencies, which indicate major unresolved welfare pressure.

evidence.claim: The dashboard reports 2022 values of 98 percent for basic drinking-water services, 90 percent for basic sanitation, and 94 percent for safely managed drinking water; it also reports 1 percent of children in extreme poverty and 16 percent child coverage by social protection floors/systems in the latest available series shown for Iran.
evidence.title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Iran (Islamic Republic of)
evidence.excerpt: The dashboard reports 2022 values of 98 percent for basic drinking-water services, 90 percent for basic sanitation, and 94 percent for safely managed drinking water; it also reports 1 percent of children in extreme poverty and 16 percent child coverage by social protection floors/systems in the latest available series shown for Iran.
evidence.source_locator: Environment and Poverty sections of the country dashboard
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official country dashboard with explicit country-year indicators and a clear data structure.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 WASH indicators and proximate child-poverty/social-protection indicators.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural/contextual rather than directly attributable; it captures inherited national conditions more than a discrete Khamenei choice.
contrary_evidence: Child social-protection coverage remains limited, so strong WASH figures do not imply broad welfare success across all domains.

evidence.claim: WHO's country data page reports 99 percent skilled-birth attendance and that DTP3 immunization coverage among one-year-olds was 99 percent and stable since 2022.
evidence.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of)
evidence.excerpt: WHO's country data page reports 99 percent skilled-birth attendance and that DTP3 immunization coverage among one-year-olds was 99 percent and stable since 2022.
evidence.source_locator: Country indicators for skilled birth attendance and DTP3 immunization coverage
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official WHO country data with explicit indicator values and a clear temporal note on stability since 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Close to the 2022 target year and useful for service-coverage baseline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural/contextual rather than directly attributable; this reflects the national health system rather than a personal Khamenei decision.
contrary_evidence: The page does not by itself show distributional equity, service quality, or ruler-level correction of failures.
